name: Onias
description: High priest at Jerusalem, whose godliness and hatred of wickedness kept the city and the law at peace; reproved Menelaus for stealing temple vessels and was lured out of sanctuary and slain by Andronicus; appeared to Judas Maccabeus in a vision, praying for Israel and presenting Jeremias the prophet

points: The holy city was inhabited with all peace, and the laws were kept very well, because of the godliness of Onias the high priest and his hatred of wickedness. Because of Onias's faith, his strength and love for God's laws, that inspired everybody else; even the kings themselves honored the place and magnified the temple with their best gifts. Seleucus king of Asia, of the line of Alexander's four generals (Lysimachus over Thrace and Asia Minor, Cassander over Macedonia and Greece, Ptolemy over Egypt, Seleucus over Babylon and Syria), bore all the costs of the sacrifices out of his own revenues.

This Simon, having been a bewrayer of the money and of his country, slandered Onias, as if he had terrified Heliodorus and been the worker of these evils. He told the Greeks that Onias did that to Heliodorus. Thus was he bold to call him a traitor, that had deserved well of the city, and tendered his own nation, and was so zealous of the laws. He called that type of a brother a traitor.
Onias was an Israelite who sought the good of all, and Simon slandered him and his own factions committed murders; the Greeks were set against our nation and used Israelites to do it.

Onias, seeing the danger of this contention, and that Apollonius as governor of Coelosyria and Phenice did rage and increase Simon's malice, went to the king: not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all, both public and private. He didn't even go there to accuse Simon. These are the characteristics of Onias III, a great and upstanding elder man.

Wherefore Menelaus, taking Andronicus apart, prayed him to get Onias into his hands; who, coming to Onias in deceit, gave him his right hand with oaths; and though he were suspected by him, yet persuaded he him to come forth of the sanctuary: whom forthwith he shut up without regard of justice. He killed Onias III, the real high priest.

In the vision Onias, who had been high priest, a virtuous and a good man, reverend in conversation, gentle in condition, well spoken, exercised from a child in all points of virtue, held up his hands and prayed for the whole body of the Jews. This is a lover of the brethren, who prayeth much for the people and for the holy city. Then Jeremiah the prophet gave Judas a holy sword, a gift from God, with which thou shalt wound the adversaries.

source.name: TIPNR, Translators Individualised Proper Names with all References, by Tyndale House Cambridge, STEPBible.org
